title: Cascading backpressure and client-retry-storm chaos harness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Validate that combined incidents — a slow external dependency (auth/model registry), a misconfigured client retry policy, and a partial region loss — do not produce a cascading failure that exhausts GPU pools, breaks SLOs, or causes uncontrolled cross-region failover.

Scope: inject coordinated faults across: 1) edge/load-balancer -> induce 20% request routing to a degraded region; 2) upstream dependency (model metadata service) injected 500-800ms tail latency; 3) client retry jitter disabled to emulate legacy SDKs; 4) synthetic high-concurrency GPU requests to force pool pressure and queue growth. Exercise circuit breakers and load-shedding guards, verify fallbacks and canary rollbacks.

Hypothesis: Without better retry/jitter defaults and global circuit breaker thresholds, a latency spike in a dependency + aggressive client retries will amplify load, driving GPU queueing and then region-level failover, producing a retry storm and elevated p99 latencies across regions. With mitigations (backoff, per-client circuit breakers, request hedging limits, and rate-limited failover), platform will avoid SLO violations or will degrade gracefully with clear fallbacks.
steps: 1) Prepare test cluster: reserve 3-region test topology with identical runtime-1.21 stack and a dedicated test customer namespace.
2) Deploy traffic generator that mimics production traffic distribution (token sizes, chat/stateful sequences, 70/30 short/long tail).
3) Toggle model-metadata service fault injection via feature-flag to add 500-800ms latency to 40% of requests and a 2% 5xx error rate.
4) Configure client SDK instances to use legacy retry policy (no jitter, aggressive 3x retry, short backoff).
5) Launch high-concurrency synthetic load targeting a heavyweight model variant to intentionally pressure GPU pools until average queue length exceeds 12 per worker or GPU utilization hits 92%.
6) At T+5m, simulate regional network partition by blackholing egress from Region B for 60 seconds (control plane still visible).
7) Observe circuit breaker behavior, cross-region failover decisions, autoscaling triggers and any global routing changes for the next 15 minutes.
8) Gradually revert injected faults and capture final state; collect traces, kernel selection logs, KV cache hit rates, and GPU queue metrics.
9) Run a second iteration with mitigations enabled: jittered exponential backoff, per-client circuit breaker thresholds, and reduced per-connection concurrency; compare metrics.
acceptance_criteria: A) No overall p99 token-service latency > 3x baseline for more than 5 minutes during fault window when mitigations are enabled.
B) Error budget burn for the simulated test customer remains under 2% of monthly budget for the day of the test when mitigations are enabled.
C) Circuit breakers trigger as expected (per-client and per-region) and prevent >70% of retry amplification observed in the control run.
D) Autoscaler does not trigger uncontrolled cross-region warm pool creation; all cross-region failovers follow routing policy and respect capacity tags.
E) Fallback model variant is served for at least 90% of requests during peak load for requests that would otherwise timeout or error.
F) Post-run logs and traces enable root-cause reconstruction within 24 hours (traces include retry count, backoff timings, and circuit breaker state transitions).
runbook: Pre-run: notify SRE on-call, calendar block 60 minutes; create snapshot of monitoring dashboards and baseline SLOs.
During-run: if cross-region failover rate exceeds 5%/min for 3 consecutive minutes, abort test and toggle global failover-disabled flag.

Abort actions: 1) stop synthetic load generator; 2) uninject dependency latency; 3) restore client SDK defaults; 4) drain and restart affected worker pools if queue depth does not decrease in 5 minutes.
Post-run: run automated data collection job (perf-collector) to upload traces, gpu-kernel logs, and routing decisions to the experiment artifact bucket.
Communication: send interim incident channel updates every 5 minutes during the run and a full post-mortem within 72 hours.
risks: Risk: synthetic load could trigger autoscaling costs or hit provider rate limits; mitigate by capping request rate and pre-authorizing cloud quota increases.
Risk: client retry storm could accidentally target production traffic if routing config misapplied; mitigate by strict namespace isolation and traffic tag checks.
Risk: latent bugs in the test harness may produce misleading results; mitigate by smoke tests and one dry-run at 10% scale.
resources: Dashboard: Console > SRE > Multi-Region Resilience > Cascading Backpressure (link saved to experiment artifact)
Perf-collector job: scripts/collect_perf.sh in infra-tools repo
